pricingStatus.freeAccountAnswer: Yes. Free accounts include one home, up to 3 household members and 20 plants, with no credit card.
pricingStatus.paidOfferAnswer: No. Free accounts are available, but the hosted site does not currently accept purchases or offer paid plans.
pricingStatus.reactivationAnswer: No. Reactivation requires a dated status decision, reviewed source and infrastructure changes, non-production verification, and a separately approved deployment.
pricingStatus.trialAnswer: A new household starts with 14 days of Garden that need no card. Nothing is charged, and when the 14 days end the household moves to the free Seedling plan on its own, keeping everything it added; each account gets one. Separately, a household’s first paid subscription begins with a 14-day trial: you are not charged until it ends, and cancelling before then costs nothing. That trial is once per household, so a household that has had one before is charged when it subscribes again.
pricingStatus.changeQuestion: Can I change or cancel later?
pricingStatus.changeAnswer: Yes. Plan changes and cancellation are self-service from Settings → Billing, which opens our payment provider's portal. Cancelling returns your household to the free Seedling tier at the end of the paid period.
pricingStatus.whereAnswer: Plan changes happen inside your account, under Settings → Billing, and are made by a household admin. Purchases are not offered in the mobile apps.
pricingStatus.dataAnswerHeld: Existing plants, household records, tasks, and care history remain available under the current plan limits. The hold does not delete user data.
pricingStatus.dataAnswerOpen: Nothing is deleted when a plan changes. If a downgrade puts you over the new caps, existing plants, members and homes stay readable and editable — only adding more is blocked until you are back under the limit. Export and your care history are never behind a plan.
pricingStatus.householdQuestion: Does everyone in my household need their own plan?
pricingStatus.householdAnswer: No. One plan covers the whole household. A household admin holds the subscription, and every member shares the same plants, tasks, and care history under it. A free home holds up to three people; Garden and Greenhouse homes have no member limit.
pricingStatus.cardQuestion: Do I need a credit card?
pricingStatus.cardAnswer: Not for a free account, and not for the 14 days of Garden a new household starts with: neither asks for a card. Starting a paid plan goes through our payment provider's checkout, which collects a card before the subscription’s trial begins; where a trial applies, nothing is charged until its 14 days end. The subscription trial is once per household, so a household that has had one before is charged when it subscribes again.

pricing.trialNote: A new household starts with 14 days of Garden, no card needed, then moves to the free plan on its own. Separately, a household’s first paid subscription begins with a 14-day trial: checkout collects a card up front, you are not charged until the 14 days are up, and cancelling before then costs nothing. pricing.whyHomesTitle: For the people who help at more than one home
pricing.whyHomesBody: Greenhouse is many homes, many hands: belong to every household you look after — your place, your parents’, the rental — and take on API access for automation.

meta.title: Family Greenhouse — Shared Plant Care & Watering Reminders
meta.descriptionOpen: Share plant watering schedules, reminders, care logs, and tasks with your household. Family Greenhouse is free for one home, up to 3 people and 20 plants.
meta.descriptionClosed: A shared care journal for household plant watering schedules, reminders, tasks, and care logs. Existing account holders can still sign in.

a.eyebrow: A garden journal for the whole house
a.subhead: Family Greenhouse is a shared care journal for the plants in your house. Everyone sees what’s due and what’s already done, so the fern doesn’t get watered twice on Tuesday and then forgotten for two weeks.

b.eyebrow: A care journal for your plants
b.subhead: Family Greenhouse keeps a watering and care schedule for every plant you own, so nothing gets missed or drowned. It works just as well for one person and a windowsill as it does for a whole household sharing the watering can.

hero.signupNote: No credit card needed — a name, email, and a password, then a one-time code we email you. About five minutes, start to finish.

mockup.label: Preview of the Family Greenhouse dashboard showing upcoming plant-care tasks and household activity.
mockup.lede: Here’s what’s happening with your plants today.

free.label: Up to 20 plants — no credit card

existing.label: Sign-in and stored care data remain available

people.label: Share one home free — unlimited on Garden

portable.label: Export plants and tasks any time

who.title: However you ended up with plants
who.description: The whole house arguing over the watering can is one story. Here are a few of the others.

sharing.label: Sharing a place
sharing.body: A partner, roommates, a family — and no one's sure who watered what. Assign tasks or leave them up for grabs, and the activity log quietly keeps score.

growing.label: A growing collection
growing.body: A few plants turned into ten. Import the spreadsheet you have been keeping, and let one dashboard hold every due date.

away.label: Away a lot
away.body: Gone for work or just the weekend. Send whoever's covering a link — no account, no app to install — and they check off what's due while you're away.

new.label: New and a little nervous
new.body: One sad succulent and a dented ego. Start with a plant that forgives you, lean on the care guides, and let the reminders do the remembering.

features.title: One schedule the whole house can see
features.description: Add a plant once and its schedule, reminders, photos, and history come along. The rest of the household sees the same thing you do.

reminders.name: Reminders per plant
reminders.description: Each plant gets its own schedule, and the nudge goes to whoever the task belongs to. The cactus stops getting watered on the fern's timetable.

shared.name: Shared, with names attached
shared.description: Everyone in the household sees what's due and what's done. The log shows who did what, which settles the watering arguments quickly.

week.name: A week you can scan
week.description: Every upcoming task on one calendar. A look on Sunday night tells you whether the week ahead is heavy or quiet.

sink.name: Works at the sink
sink.description: Installs to your phone like any app. Mark a task done with one thumb, add a note, get back to the watering can.

memory.name: A memory for each plant
memory.description: Notes, photos, and the full care log live with the plant. When leaves yellow, you check what happened instead of guessing.

yours.name: Yours to keep
yours.description: Your household's data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and you can export your profile, plants and tasks as JSON or CSV whenever you like.

cover.name: Someone else can cover
cover.description: Send a link before you travel — no account, no app, nothing to install. They see what's due and tap it done. The Away Kit (Garden and up) stretches coverage to 90 days and adds a printable handoff brief.

beyond.title: More than a reminder app
beyond.description: The shared schedule is where it starts. These are the parts you grow into.

weather.label: Weather-aware nudges
weather.body: Add your location and the app offers to skip a watering when rain or a cold snap is on the way.

leaf.label: Check a leaf from a photo
leaf.body: Upload a struggling leaf and get a read on what might be going wrong.

cutting.label: Share a cutting
cutting.body: Propagating? Track which plant came from which, and send a friend a link to the cutting you are passing on.

reminders.label: Reminders where you'll see them
reminders.body: Browser or email, on the day a task is due. Set quiet hours and every reminder waits for them.

year.label: A year, looked back on
year.body: Come December, see what the household actually did: plants added, tasks finished, the whole season on Garden and Greenhouse, the last 30 days on the free plan.

add.title: Add your plants
add.description: A name and a photo will do. Pick a watering rhythm yourself or start from a species suggestion.

invite.title: Invite your household
invite.description: Send one link. Whoever lives with you joins and sees the same plants and the same task list.

split.title: Split the work
split.description: Assign tasks, or let whoever's home claim them. Reminders go out, the history fills in.

care.title: Know what you’re getting into
care.body: The care guides are honest about the parts the plant-shop label skips: how often it actually needs water, what the brown tips are telling you, and whether it’s safe around a cat or a curious toddler. Worth a read before the plant comes home.
